title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab

content.caseIdentity: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab, (1980) 2 SCC 565
content.facts: The Supreme Court considered applications for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and the scope of the power of the High Court and Court of Session.
questionsBeforeCourt: What is the scope of the power to grant anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?
content.ratioDecidendi: The power under Section 438 is not to be confined by rigid, inflexible rules; the High Court and Court of Session have broad discretion to grant anticipatory bail subject to judicially appropriate conditions.
content.holding: Anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC is a judicial safeguard against unnecessary deprivation of personal liberty; the High Court and Court of Session have wide powers that should not be burdened with unwarranted restrictions.
content.relevance: Foundational Constitution Bench ruling on anticipatory bail principles.

sources.bench: Y.V. Chandrachud, C.J.; P.N. Bhagwati, N.L. Untwalia, R.S. Pathak and O. Chinnappa Reddy, JJ.
sources.evidenceNote: Official Supreme Court judgment confirms the case identity, 9 April 1980 judgment date, Constitution Bench composition and the scope of anticipatory-bail discretion under Section 438 CrPC.
